title: Self-information
summary: Self-information assigns a logarithmic surprise to an event of positive probability.

context.note: Revision 2 narrows the broad title and supplies the missing logarithm-base condition.

assumptions.text: A probability space and an event E of positive probability are fixed.

content.plain: Within a probability model, a less probable event carries more self-information when surprise is measured logarithmically.
content.exact: For an event E with 0<P(E)≤1 and a real base b>1, its self-information is I_b(E):=−log_b(P(E)). The unit is the bit when b=2 and the nat when b=e.
content.example: Either result of a fair coin toss has self-information 1 bit.
content.caveat: Self-information is model-relative and is not identical to meaning, knowledge, usefulness, evidence, or truth.

verification.method: QEVA 0.5 protocol audit corrected scope, assumptions, and dependency semantics; no formal proof is claimed.

provenance.creator: QEVA 0.5 mathematical protocol audit
provenance.source_note: Adds b>1 and disambiguates self-information from the much broader word information. This is an original QEVA formulation and remains subject to independent review.
